title: Finding files and metadata
intro: Work from home. Use **`find`** for traversal. These exercises inspect the container's Linux filesystem: **`/etc`**, **`/var/log`**, **`/usr/local`**, **`/srv`**, and **`/var/spool`**.

questions.prompt: How many regular files exist anywhere under **`/etc/course-lab/`**? Give just the count.
List every file under **`/var/log/course`** whose base name is exactly `backup.log`. Give paths relative to `/var/log/course`, sorted, one per line.
List every regular file under **`/var/log/course`** whose name contains `.log` anywhere in it, regardless of case. Give paths relative to `/var/log/course`, sorted, one per line.
List all subdirectories of **`/srv/www/app`** at most two directory levels below the root, excluding the root itself. Give paths relative to `/srv/www/app`, sorted.
List all empty regular files under **`/etc/course-lab`**. Give paths relative to `/etc/course-lab`, sorted.
Count the `.log` files under **`/var/log/course`** but skip the entire `archive/` subdirectory tree. Give just the integer.
What is the combined byte count of all `.log` files under **`/var/log/course`**, excluding those inside `archive/`? Give just the integer.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
find /var/log/course \( -path '/var/log/course/archive*' -prune \) -o -type f -name '*.log*' -print0 | xargs -0 cat | wc -c
```

Piping through `cat` before `wc -c` gives a single total without filename labels.

questions.prompt: Find all `.yaml` files anywhere under **`/etc/course-lab`** and count their lines. Report in `wc -l` format (count and filename).
Print the one line inside the hidden flag file under **`/etc/course-lab`** using `find` — without typing the literal path `.cache/flag` in your command.

There is a file named **`--odd-name.conf`** under `/etc/course-lab`. Count its lines using `find` to locate it and a byte or line counter to measure it, taking care that the leading dashes don't confuse the tool.
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```bash
find /etc/course-lab -name '--odd-name.conf' -print0 | xargs -0 -- wc -l
```

`xargs --` signals end of `xargs` options so the leading-dash filename isn't misinterpreted as a flag.

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes
- Compose `find` predicates for name, type, time, size, permissions, and logical operators.
- Use `-exec`, `-ok`, `-delete` safely; prefer `-print0` with `xargs -0`.
- Compare `find` to database-backed search where appropriate.
- Understand capability gaps on macOS BSD `find` vs GNU `find`.

## Scope

**In scope:** traversal, filtering, action primitives, interaction with `xargs`. **Out of scope:** `locate`/`plocate` implementation details of `updatedb` (mention only); content search (see Basics — grep topics).
